If that plan looks good I’ll mark the HubSpot deal and coordinate a follow-up with Karthik.

Rishi — thanks for the recap. That matches our notes.

I attached our standard vendor security questionnaire and a rough network diagram. A few quick notes:

- Procurement wants a vendor risk assessment form completed; I’ve looped procurement@moneytree.com on this thread.
- For scope: initially we only need Redwood to handle inference for non-PII transactional data (tokenized IDs + product descriptions). We will rule out full name / SSN / payment card data for now.
- Key management: we use AWS KMS with customer-managed keys for encryption of at-rest artifacts. We need to confirm whether Redwood can integrate with our KMS or if we’ll handle encryption at rest on our side.

I’m attaching: moneytree_vendor_questionnaire.pdf, moneytree-network-diagram.png

We’re aiming to get procurement sign-off within 2–3 weeks pending questionnaire answers and DPA review.

Regards,
Samir Khan

samir.khan@moneytree.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@moneytree.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro call — security questionnaire & buying roles (MoneyTree)

Thanks — a few clarifying questions from a security/infra lens so we scope correctly before the intake call: 

1) Systems in-scope: you mentioned inference for non-PII transactional data. Can you confirm the upstream systems sending requests (API gateway, internal service names) and whether any storage of request traces/logs will contain user-identifiable fields?

2) KV cache / prefix caching: do you anticipate long-running conversations or mostly one-off inference per request? We have different cache/retention guidance depending on that pattern.

3) KMS integration: if MoneyTree requires CMKs, do you have an existing AWS account and key policy we should reference? Alternatively, we can offer a configuration where Redwood encrypts at rest with our keys and you control access via a dedicated VPC + peering.

4) Egress / allowed regions: which cloud regions are in scope (us-east-1 only or multi-region)?

I’ll draft concise answers to the vendor questionnaire once we have those details. If the procurement timeline is tight, we can prepare a short security summary (2–3 pages) that highlights control mappings to common frameworks (SOC2/ISO) to accelerate legal review.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Solutions & Security Ops Lead
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@moneytree.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, procurement@moneytree.com
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 12:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro call — security questionnaire & buying roles (MoneyTree)

Karthik — thanks, good questions. Answers below: 

1) Upstream systems: calls will come from our internal inference-proxy service (infraprod-01.moneytree.local). No request bodies will include full user identifiers; we will tokenize and send only product/event IDs + metadata.

2) Cache pattern: mostly one-off inference per request; occasional multi-turn sessions for product recommendation flows, but those are short-lived (TTL < 2 minutes).

3) KMS: we have a customer-managed KMS in account MT-PROD (policy available on request). Procurement prefers CMK integration for any persistent storage that holds derived artifacts. If Redwood needs to see the key policy, procurement@moneytree.com can share.

4) Regions: us-east-1 primarily; we may add eu-west-1 later but that is out of scope for initial pilot.

Procurement note: procurement@moneytree.com — once we have Redwood's questionnaire answers and the short security summary Karthik mentioned, we can open the vendor packet. Targeting procurement review window of 10 business days from when we receive those artifacts.

Happy to jump on the intake call next Tue. Samir

Samir Khan
Senior Security Engineer | MoneyTree
